chapter: Chicago pianists and New Orleans bands
title: Tommy Ladner, Cafe de Champions and the Elite band
summary: Other early trumpeters, and how he met and played with Tommy Ladner at Jack Johnson's Cafe de Champions around 1911-12.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Do you remember a group that came up here with Manuel Perez and Lorenzo Teo? Do you remember? No, I didn't remember that. Or another, Tig Chambers, I think, was up here pretty early. Do you remember a cornet player, Tig Chambers?
No, I didn't know him. No. First trumpet players was Freddie Chambers and Tommy Ladner.
About four or six pieces, around six pieces. You played with Tommy, of course. You made that record. Can you tell me the first time you ever heard Tommy and when you played with him?
Well, I met Tommy, I guess, must have been around 11 or 12. Around 11 or 12. Around the days of when Jack Johnson opened up. 41 West 31st Street.
What did he have, a club or saloon or something?

41 West 31st Street. Ed Harden was the first piano player he had. And I was corresponding with a friend of mine that plays beyond in Louisville, named Taylor, Will Taylor. He's a New York guy. He ended up a good musician. He studied music in quite a good arranger around New York. That was before Benny Carter.
Benny Carter was a great musician. Great musician. Great arranger.
When did you play with Tommy Ladner first? Do you remember?
Oh, that was around 11. Tommy used to bring it. Tommy didn't have any band. He'd come around there and play with us. I don't know. The band really wasn't one of those cafe bands.
It wasn't mine. It wasn't mine. It wasn't anyone else.
It just said that. It belonged to the cafe.
